items.text: Homo sapiens as a species is defined by its genome. <break time="0.8s" /> Unlike a digital document that can be flawlessly copied, again and again, without a single character missing or out of place, genomes are subject to random mutations and copying errors as the information is passed from parents to offspring. <break time="0.8s" /> This comes on top of the genetic lottery as we inherit about half of our dads genes and half of our moms, but which of our dads genes and which of our moms genes we inherit is random, like a deck of shuffled cards. <break time="0.8s" /> We all carry variants of natures instruction manual for who we can become, differing in roughly one out of every thousand nucleotides. <break time="0.8s" /> These copying errors are not a bug but a feature, as offspring with diverse genomes are the raw material shaped by the forces of evolution by natural selection. <break time="0.8s" /> Some may be better adapted to a particular ecological niche, while most are either neutral or do worse. <break time="0.8s" /> The former will have a higher chance, and the latter a lower one, of surviving and therefore passing on their genome to the next generation.
